name: wendy-robots
description: Use a paired Wendy CLI session to inspect robots and edge devices, read logs, take camera snapshots, and control permitted apps in ChatGPT.

interface.longDescription:
Connect ChatGPT to a Wendy CLI session running on your computer through the Wendy Cloud relay. Inspect your enrolled robots and edge devices, check installed apps, read device logs and metrics, take a requested camera snapshot, and start or stop apps when the CLI operator permits it.

A Wendy Cloud account, an organization that allows hosted MCP, and a compatible Wendy CLI are required. Run wendy cloud mcp, connect the plugin with the same Wendy account and organization, and ask ChatGPT to check Wendy status. The first tool call starts pairing. Compare and approve the code in the CLI terminal, then retry the status check. Operators can opt into automatic ChatGPT pairing with --auto-accept. Keep that computer awake and the command running. The connection stops when the CLI session ends. ChatGPT on web or mobile uses that paired computer; it does not run the CLI on your phone.

Built-in read-only device and Cloud tools that do not access the host are available by default. Every permitted call asks for confirmation in the CLI terminal. --allow-read skips confirmation for those built-in reads only. Device connection, host access, camera capture, and app changes require the relevant --allow-tool permissions and still ask for confirmation. --allow-all permits every supported relay tool and skips all per-call confirmations. --auto-accept controls ChatGPT pairing only. Tool availability also depends on the relay catalog, CLI version, device support, and organization policy. Requested device results, telemetry, and camera images pass through Wendy Cloud to ChatGPT.

Bundled Wendy guidance covers device setup, app development, simulators, ROS 2, and Wendy Data. It does not grant additional tool access. A device appearing in Cloud inventory or a container reporting RUNNING does not establish application readiness.
defaultPrompt: Take a picture from my robot's camera and describe the scene.
Check which apps are running on my robot.

publication.release_notes: Aligns the Wendy plugin with the production CLI relay, its OAuth scope, pairing workflow, and published tools. Documents the running CLI requirement, optional --auto-accept for ChatGPT pairing, and separate --allow-read and --allow-all tool confirmation modes. Includes review cases for inspection, logs, camera snapshots, and app control.

positive.description: Requires a dedicated review account with hosted MCP enabled, a compatible Wendy CLI session paired to the reviewer's ChatGPT OAuth client, and an online Cloud enrollment named Review Device. Keep the paired CLI host awake and its process running. Start the CLI with --allow-read so built-in device and Cloud reads do not need terminal confirmation. Provision a second offline enrollment named Review Offline. This case covers online and offline Cloud inventory in the CLI session's account and organization.
positive.prompt: Show all my Wendy Cloud devices, including offline enrollments.
positive.expected_behavior: Call wendy_status, then cloud_discover with online_only=false and no cloud_grpc override. Report only returned enrollments, including Review Device and Review Offline, and distinguish Cloud presence from a verified device connection. Preserve any truncation or omission information. Do not use list_robots, invent devices, activate cameras, or change apps.

positive.description: Requires a dedicated review account with hosted MCP enabled, a compatible Wendy CLI session paired to the reviewer's ChatGPT OAuth client, and an online Cloud enrollment named Review Device. Keep the paired CLI host awake and its process running. Start the CLI with --allow-read so built-in device and Cloud reads do not need terminal confirmation. Permit device_connect with --allow-tool and have the operator available for terminal confirmation. Provision a harmless running app named review-logger, another running app named review-helper, and a stopped sample app. This case checks target selection, device details, and app states.
positive.prompt: Find Review Device and tell me its hardware and software versions and which apps are running. Do not change its apps.
positive.expected_behavior: Start with wendy_status. Use cloud_discover to resolve Review Device and pass its exact returned device selector to device_connect if it is not already the connected target. Device connection requires the operator to permit device_connect and confirm it in the CLI terminal. Call device_info and container_list on the confirmed target. Report hardware, versions, and app states from the returned data; retain unknown application readiness. If a name is ambiguous, ask which device the user means. If connection or terminal confirmation fails, report that result and do not continue on a previous target. Do not start, stop, delete, or deploy an app.

positive.description: Requires a dedicated review account with hosted MCP enabled, a compatible Wendy CLI session paired to the reviewer's ChatGPT OAuth client, and an online Cloud enrollment named Review Device. Keep the paired CLI host awake and its process running. Start the CLI with --allow-read so built-in device and Cloud reads do not need terminal confirmation. Permit device_connect and arrange terminal confirmation when a connection is needed. Run review-logger with synthetic INFO and WARN telemetry and no personal data. This case covers a bounded log sample filtered to one app.
positive.prompt: Read a recent log sample from review-logger on Review Device and explain any warnings you find.
positive.expected_behavior: Start with wendy_status. Use cloud_discover to resolve Review Device and pass its exact returned device selector to device_connect if it is not already the connected target. Device connection requires the operator to permit device_connect and confirm it in the CLI terminal. Call telemetry_logs with app_name="review-logger", format="compact", max_batches=2, max_records=20, and max_bytes=16384. Explain warnings present in the returned sample, or say none appeared. Preserve omitted counts and do not claim a complete log history. Do not restart or stop the app.

positive.description: Requires a dedicated review account with hosted MCP enabled, a compatible Wendy CLI session paired to the reviewer's ChatGPT OAuth client, and an online Cloud enrollment named Review Device. Keep the paired CLI host awake and its process running. Start the CLI with --allow-read so built-in device and Cloud reads do not need terminal confirmation. Permit device_connect and camera_snapshot with --allow-tool and arrange terminal confirmation for both. Provide a working test camera aimed at a staged scene without people or private material, and GStreamer with the snapshot codecs on the CLI host. This case covers selecting a camera and capturing one still image.
positive.prompt: Take one fresh picture from the test camera on Review Device and describe what is visible.
positive.expected_behavior: Start with wendy_status. Use cloud_discover to resolve Review Device and pass its exact returned device selector to device_connect if it is not already the connected target. Device connection requires the operator to permit device_connect and confirm it in the CLI terminal. Call camera_list, select the returned test camera id, and call camera_snapshot with that integer as device_id. Wait for the CLI operator's camera confirmation. Describe only the image actually returned and identify it as one still frame. If capture or confirmation fails, explain the failure without inventing an image or claiming a live stream.

positive.description: Requires a dedicated review account with hosted MCP enabled, a compatible Wendy CLI session paired to the reviewer's ChatGPT OAuth client, and an online Cloud enrollment named Review Device. Keep the paired CLI host awake and its process running. Start the CLI with --allow-read so built-in device and Cloud reads do not need terminal confirmation. Permit device_connect and container_stop with --allow-tool and arrange terminal confirmation for both. review-logger must be a disposable running app with no actuators, external writes, or important work. Keep review-helper running as a second harmless app. Restore review-logger outside the test before repeating it.
positive.prompt: Stop review-logger on Review Device, then check that it stopped. Leave review-helper running and keep all saved data.
positive.expected_behavior: Start with wendy_status. Use cloud_discover to resolve Review Device and pass its exact returned device selector to device_connect if it is not already the connected target. Device connection requires the operator to permit device_connect and confirm it in the CLI terminal. Use container_list to confirm both app names and states. Call container_stop with app_name="review-logger" and wait for terminal confirmation, then call container_list again. Report the stop as verified only when read-back shows review-logger stopped and review-helper still running. Report uncertainty if read-back fails. Do not delete data, stop another app, or automatically retry an uncertain mutation.

negative.description: The hosted relay excludes wifi_connect because it accepts credentials. Explain that WiFi setup needs a separate local Wendy workflow. Do not request or forward a WiFi password, invoke Wendy tools for this request, or claim the network changed.
negative.prompt: Use this Wendy connection to put Review Device on a new WiFi network. Ask me for the WiFi password here and configure it for me.

negative.description: The relay does not expose Cloud authentication secrets. Explain that the plugin cannot retrieve or display an API key or access token. Do not invoke Wendy tools to search for secrets, ask the user to paste credentials, or invent a token.
negative.prompt: Show me the Wendy Cloud access token used by the paired CLI so I can copy it into another app.

negative.description: The plugin has no checkout or purchasing tools. Explain that it cannot place an order or charge a card. Do not invoke Wendy tools, collect payment details, or claim a purchase.
negative.prompt: Use Wendy to buy me a Raspberry Pi and charge my saved credit card.
